title: The Five Types That Destroy Reader Trust
use_cases: Use when auditing a draft for narrative consistency
Implement when developing a world-building style guide
Configure when tracking character arcs and information asymmetry
Use when identifying why a reader may lose immersion
Implement when resolving complex subplots or chronological sequences
content:
You've seen lists of "common plot holes" that are vague and unhelpful. Here are the five specific categories that actually matter, with examples you'll recognize from your own drafts:

1. Character inconsistencies — personality shifts, forgotten abilities, physical description changes
2. Timeline errors — events happening in impossible sequences, seasons that don't track
3. Forgotten threads — subplots introduced and never resolved, Chekhov's gun that never fires
4. World contradictions — magic system rules that change, geography that shifts between chapters
5. Character knowledge mistakes — a character acting on information they haven't learned yet

Every one of these stems from the same root cause: lost context.
